newsitem.title: USA: SPX to build die-casting plant in Indiana.
newsitem.headline: SPX to build die-casting plant in Indiana.

text.p: SPX Corp said Friday its Contech division plans to build a 45,000-square-foot, $8.4 million aluminum die-casting facility in Pierceton, Ind.
Construction will start immediately and the facility is expected to be operating by year-end. The plant will initially employ about 48 people.

The Indiana Department of Commerce will offer SPX a development incentive package that includes a training grant. The grant will reimburse the company up to 50 percent of the cost of training people who will work at the facility. The package includes an Economic Development for a Growing Economy (EDGE) tax credit of up to $555,950. EDGE provides tax credits to companies that make a significant capital and jobs investment in Indiana.

"Aluminum castings are rapidly replacing conventional heavier metal castings in automotive applications," said Gary Walker, president of Contech division. Contech has won contracts to provide power steering component castings to various vehicle manufacturers for upcoming model years. The new capacity at Pierceton is required to meet these contracts.
